figure1.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Edit this existing portrait scientific teaser. Preserve its precise factual content, three vertically stacked panels, all entities and answers, all arrows and functional relations, portrait 3:4 aspect ratio, and compact single-column purpose. Keep all existing labels and wording, including "Walter II of Avesnes", "James of Avesnes", "Arsuf", "Native: Avesnes", "Address recoverable", "Paragraph access", "Local reading", "CoReTrace (Ours)", and "Composed answer: Arsuf". Keep the same three panel titles "(a) Correct hops, failed composition", "(b) Access and reading interact", "(c) Mechanistic repair". Changes required: make ALL typography clean, crisp Arial/Helvetica-like sans-serif (panel titles bold); all surfaces flat white or pale blue, pale orange, pale purple, or gray, with thin black outlines. Remove green/teal everywhere. Replace all teal in attention-head squares and final correct answer strip with blue #1F77B4 (pale #EAF2F8). Replace all green checks with blue checks. Make the answer entity Arsuf pale orange #FFF1DD. Use bright but restrained red #D62728 for the incorrect Native answer and X, pale red fill #FBE9E7. Keep address purple #9467BD (pale #F0EAF7). Gray #EEEEEE for neutrals. No shadows, gradient fills, textures, or decorative clipart. Thin light-gray horizontal panel dividers. Improve alignment and keep generous gap between labels and arrows, all readable at a 3.25-inch printed width. Do not introduce statistical plots, extra claims, words, numbers, or new structure.
figure1.style: Sans-serif labels; blue/orange/purple; white background; conceptual illustrations. Numerical plots are generated from experiment outputs.

figure2.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a NEW conceptual overview illustration for Figure 2 of an ICML mechanistic interpretability paper. It introduces the actual diagnostic design; it contains no empirical plots, no invented measurements, and no numeric heatmap. Wide landscape, approximately 2.65:1, high resolution, clean white background. Three compact, equally tall panels in one row, separated by thin light-gray vertical rules. Scientific journal aesthetic: flat fills, thin black arrows, crisp Arial/Helvetica-like sans-serif labels, bold panel headings, compact readable text. Palette: blue #1F77B4 with pale #EAF2F8; orange #FF7F0E with pale #FFF1DD; purple #9467BD with pale #F0EAF7; neutral gray #EEEEEE. No green or teal, shadows, gradients, decorative icons, caption, figure number, or overall banner.

LEFT PANEL:
Heading exactly "(a) Locate evidence-access heads".
A shared small stack of paragraph sheets under the label "Same context".
Two adjacent question boxes, one labeled "Direct-hop query" and one labeled "Composed query". Both point to a small schematic attention-head grid, only three blue squares among gray squares. Under the grid write "Paired attention gap".
A short arrow leads to a compact blue outlined box labeled "Selected heads".
Bottom line: "Selected vs. random knockout".
This is a conceptual head-selection sketch, with no axis ticks, layer values, performance numbers, or measured heatmap.

MIDDLE PANEL:
Heading exactly "(b) Separate access and reading".
Centered formula "Aₚ = mₚ ρₚ".
Below is a clean 2-by-2 factorial design with clear short column headings "Receiver pattern" and "Direct-hop pattern", and two short row headings "Native mass" and "Calibrated mass".
The four equal cells are labeled exactly:
top left "Native", top right "Pattern",
bottom left "Mass", bottom right "Both".
Use pale gray for Native, pale orange for Pattern, pale blue for Mass, pale purple for Both. Include a simple token strip of five small boxes under each cell label, purely schematic; do not make a statistical chart.
Beneath the matrix write "Receiver values + output projection".
Bottom line: "2 × 2 causal intervention".
Keep all matrix labels legible and non-overlapping.

RIGHT PANEL:
Heading exactly "(c) Test local content use".
Two columns titled "Original" and "Exchanged".
In the original column place two small paragraph cards labelled "Bridge A" and "Bridge B", each with short generic text: "relation: x" and "relation: y".
In the exchanged column repeat the same cards with "relation: y" for Bridge A and "relation: x" for Bridge B.
Highlight x consistently in blue and y consistently in orange. Show slim crossing arrows between the highlighted values to convey their reciprocal exchange, routing them through the blank gap between columns.
Below write "Same question and word counts".
Bottom line on two lines: "Does the answer follow\nthe changed value?".
This panel illustrates a relational value exchange, not a replacement of entire paragraphs.

Align panel bottoms and headings. Use large enough text for a 6.75-inch-wide paper figure. Render all text exactly, with no extra words. Preserve a restrained, conventional scientific figure appearance.
figure2.style: Sans-serif labels; blue/orange/purple; white background; conceptual illustrations. Numerical plots are generated from experiment outputs.

figure3.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a NEW conceptual method overview for an ICML paper, Figure 3. Wide landscape about 2.65:1, high-resolution, clean white background. Flat conventional academic diagram, sharp Arial/Helvetica-like sans-serif type, compact readable labels, thin black outlines and arrows, panel headings bold, pale blue #EAF2F8, blue #1F77B4, orange #FF7F0E, pale orange #FFF1DD, purple #9467BD, pale purple #F0EAF7, gray #EEEEEE. No green, teal, drop shadows, gradients, decorative clipart, figure number or caption. Match the visual family of a classic scientific framework diagram. This is a conceptual workflow, not a quantitative chart.

TWO horizontal rows, thin gray rule between rows.

TOP ROW title "(a) Mechanism-guided preparation".
Three aligned modules in a left-to-right sequence:
1. Title "Adapt selected heads". A short line "Composed-answer training". Four equal orange outlined, pale-orange boxes marked exactly "Q", "K", "V", "O", all identically styled because all four are trained. Under them a short line "Selected projection slices".
2. Title "Restore native contributions". Two small horizontal token strips: the first labelled "Input prefill" contains a mixture of blue and orange token squares; the second labelled "Cached decode" contains only orange token squares. A short line below "Native V and/or O at fixed prefill positions". A tiny but legible key: blue square "Native", orange square "Adapted". The strips are conceptual and have no numerical axis.
3. Title "Fit the address readout". A short line "Adapted-model attention features". Centered formula "s(p) = wᵀh(p)" in a pale-purple rectangular box. Under it "Training bridge labels".
Use slim arrows from module 1 to 2 and module 2 to 3. The latter arrow represents extraction of attention features under the restored adapted model. Keep modules separated so no arrow crosses text.

BOTTOM ROW title "(b) Evidence-guided inference".
A left-to-right workflow:
- A small stack of document outlines plus a question symbol, labelled "Context + question".
- Arrow to a compact title-link graph (one root node above two candidate nodes), labelled "Title-link candidates".
- Arrow branches into three vertically stacked compact rectangular boxes:
"One: use candidate" in pale blue
"Several: attention readout" in pale purple
"Empty: retain context" in pale gray.
- The first and second branches converge into two document outlines labelled "Root + bridge".
- Arrow from these documents into a blue outlined model rectangle labelled "Restored adapted model".
- Arrow from the model to a pale-orange box labelled "Answer".
- The bottom Empty branch bypasses the two-document selection and goes directly into the model via a clear thin gray path below the documents.
Show one dashed purple link from the fitted readout in the top row to ONLY the "Several: attention readout" box in the bottom row, routed through the separator corridor without crossing words.
Show one dashed blue link from top restoration module to the bottom model, routed separately through the row-separator corridor without crossing any labels. The two carry-over links should remain visually separate.
Compact footer text exactly "Original paragraph text • Original question • Greedy answer generation".
All text exactly spelled. Large enough to read at a printed width of 6.75 inches. Balanced compact spacing, no huge empty card areas.
figure3.style: Sans-serif labels; blue/orange/purple; white background; conceptual illustrations. Numerical plots are generated from experiment outputs.
